newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower but volume remains light.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower but volume remains light.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices drifted to its lowest level in more than two months on Thursday amid continued long liquidation by speculators, but scattered trade buying provided a buffer at the lows, dealers said.

After gapping lower at the open, the market hovered in weaker territory throughout the day. Some trade buying surfaced in the $1,390-1,395 area basis July, but overall interest in the market was scant.
"The market is still suffering a technical breakdown," said one trader. "It's chart driven in the short-term."

Benchmark July futures fell $9 a tonne, to $1,391, near the bottom of today's 1,390-1,404 range. Today's close marked the first time since early March that July has settled below the widely-watched $1,400 level.

Most traders shrugged off news the International Cocoa Organization cut its estimate of the world's cocoa supply deficit. The ICCO put the shortfall at 115,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 crop year, down from a 225,000 deficit seen earlier this year.
